replacements.from: In fact the three tensors 8 Similarly, we saw that a rank-1 tensor, i.e., what we called in lecture 1 an abstract vector, has a contravariant form and a covariant form.
replacements.to:
In fact the three tensors \(g_{mn}\), \(g^{mn}\), and \(g_m^n\) are really just a single tensor written in three forms\footnote{Similarly, we saw that a rank-1 tensor, i.e., what we called in lecture 1 an abstract vector, has a contravariant form and a covariant form.}: the first with two covariant indices, the second with two contravariant indices, and the third with a covariant and a contravariant index.

\emph{The fact that there is a metric tensor with downstairs indices and a metric tensor with upstairs indices will play an important role.}

So far everything we have seen on tensors was easy. It is essentially learning and getting accustomed to the notation.

This lecture was about tensor algebra. The next lecture deals with tensor calculus: in particular with the dark art of parallel transporting tensors, differentiating tensors, and most importantly building a curvature tensor from the derivatives.

It is the curvature tensor that will tell us if a geometry is flat or curved, and in general relativity whether a gravitational field exerts tidal forces.
